findings.claim: Entu server-side rights model, ground-truthed from entu-api source (~/projects/entu-api), gives an EXACT, asymmetric rights requirement per HTTP verb that explains both Mechanism A and Mechanism B: (1) POST entity/{id} requires EDITOR (not owner) on the entity being posted to for a plain non-rightType property write, PLUS — only for property.type === '_parent' specifically — EXPANDER rights on the REFERENCED (target/new-parent) entity, checked in validatePropertyTypes. (2) DELETE property/{id} requires EDITOR on the owning entity for ordinary properties, but for property.type === '_parent' the delete route's OWN rightTypes list (which, unlike the POST route's rightTypes list, INCLUDES '_parent') additionally demands OWNER (not just editor) on the owning entity, PLUS EXPANDER on the OLD parent entity referenced by the value being deleted.
findings.evidence: entity.js:21-29 (POST-side rightTypes, no `_parent`): `const rightTypes = ['_noaccess','_viewer','_expander','_editor','_owner','_sharing','_inheritrights']`; entity.js:83-121 checkEntityAccess: editor-only gate at :104-111 (`entity.private?._editor`), owner-only-if-rightType gate at :113-121 (does not fire for plain `_parent`); entity.js:235-262 validatePropertyTypes' `_parent`-specific gate: looks up `property.reference` (the NEW target), requires `entu.userStr` in that target's `private._expander` (:254), else 400 'User not in parent _owner, _editor nor _expander property' (:256-261). property/[_id]/index.delete.js:56-65 (DELETE-side rightTypes, INCLUDES `_parent`): `const rightTypes = ['_noaccess','_viewer','_expander','_editor','_owner','_sharing','_parent','_inheritrights']`; :129-136 editor gate on the owning entity; :138-145 owner gate that FIRES for `_parent` because it's in this route's rightTypes (`if (rightTypes.includes(property.type) && !owners.includes(entu.userStr))`); :154-179 additional `_parent`-specific gate on the OLD referenced parent's `_expander` bucket.

findings.claim: This confirms Mechanism A precisely: reparentSection's POST (needs only EDITOR on the moved section + EXPANDER on the new target) can succeed for a limited-rights user, while its DELETE of the old _parent value (needs OWNER on the moved section, per delete.js's rightTypes including _parent) can fail for that same user if they hold editor-but-not-owner on their own section. When the DELETE throws inside reparentSection, the exception propagates out of the `await reparentSection(...)` call at roster/+page.svelte:1660 BEFORE line 1661 executes, so `moveLanded` stays `false` even though the POST (the actual _parent move) already landed on the server.
findings.evidence: sectionActions.ts:530-539: the DELETE loop's failure throws `SectionReparentPartialError('reparent', 0, 0, ...)` from INSIDE reparentSection, after the POST at :519-529 has already succeeded. roster/+page.svelte:1658-1668: `let moveLanded = false; try { await reparentSection(cfg, node.id, newParentId); moveLanded = true; ... } catch (e) { ... reparentPartial = moveLanded; ... }` — moveLanded is only set on line 1661, reachable ONLY if reparentSection resolves without throwing; a throw from its internal DELETE step means this line is never reached, so `reparentPartial` at :1684 is `false`.

findings.claim: Banner copy shown for mechanism A (moveLanded=false due to the inner DELETE failure): reparentPartial is false, so the template renders m.roster_section_reorder_failed() — the 'couldn't be saved' copy — NOT roster_section_reparent_partial(). This is the exact lying banner the ticket describes: the _parent POST already landed server-side (with the old value left un-deleted, i.e. a dangling duplicate _parent), but the UI says nothing landed.

findings.claim: After the error, the page DOES refetch: performReparent's catch block calls `listSections(cfg)` and, if the collective-selection generation hasn't changed, replaces `sections` with the fresh server-derived tree; only if that refetch itself throws does it fall back to the pre-move local snapshot (`before`).

findings.claim: What the refetch renders for a half-landed move (mechanism A) is itself misleading in a second, independent way: after mechanism A, the moved section's entity now holds TWO active `_parent` values of entity_type 'section' (the old one the DELETE failed to remove, plus the new one the POST added). listSections builds each node's parentId with `.find()`, which silently picks whichever matching `_parent` value appears FIRST in the array the Entu GET response returns for that entity — there is no merge/conflict handling, no indication to the caller that duplicate parents exist.
findings.evidence: sectionData.ts:112: `const parentId = (r._parent ?? []).find((p) => p.entity_type === 'section')?.reference ?? null;` — same `.find()`-picks-first pattern at :117 for dbEntityId. I did NOT verify what order Entu's entity GET route returns multi-valued properties in (creation order vs. some other order), so which of the two _parent values (old vs new) actually wins on screen after the refetch is [unverified] — but the mechanism (silent pick-one-of-many, no duplicate detection) is confirmed from source.

findings.claim: Mechanism B (outdent/unindent-to-top target = org/db entity) is explained by the SAME validatePropertyTypes gate as above, but hitting the POST itself rather than the DELETE: writing `_parent = target.dbEntityId` requires the caller to be in that db/org entity's `_expander` bucket. A limited-rights member ordinarily has no rights property at all on the collective's own database entity, so the POST step of reparentSection (not just the DELETE) is expected to 400 for this case — meaning for pure unindent-to-top, `moveLanded` correctly stays false and the 'nothing landed' banner is accurate, unlike mechanism A's indent case.
findings.evidence: entity.js:235-262 (validatePropertyTypes' _parent gate, described above) applies identically regardless of whether the target is a section or the database entity — `_parent`'s reference-target lookup and _expander check has no special-case for entity_type; roster/+page.svelte:1650 confirms unindent-to-top's newParentId literally IS `target.dbEntityId`, fed straight into the same `reparentSection` call used for indent.

findings.claim: reorderSections' own rights bar is lower than reparentSection's DELETE step: `display_order` is not a system (`_`-prefixed) property, so neither route's rightTypes list ever includes it — both its POST and its DELETE only require EDITOR (not owner) on each sibling section being renumbered. So a partial renumber failure (SectionReparentPartialError step:'renumber') most plausibly means the user lacks EDITOR on some section in the destination sibling group, not the owner-specific gate that trips up the reparent DELETE.
findings.evidence: sectionActions.ts:352-361 (renumber POST body `[{ type: 'display_order', number }]`) and :373-384 (renumber DELETE loop) target `entity/{id}` / `property/{valueId}` for `display_order`, a plain non-underscore property type; entity.js:170-175 and delete.js:105-110 both only special-case property types starting with `_`, so `display_order` never triggers either route's owner-tier or _parent-specific gates — confirmed by reading systemPropertyValueTypes/rightTypes lists in both files, which list only `_`-prefixed names.

risks: The exact order Entu's entity GET endpoint returns multi-valued property arrays in (which determines which of two duplicate _parent values `.find()` in sectionData.ts:112 actually picks after a mechanism-A half-landed move) was not verified from source in this pass — flagged [unverified] in the findings above. Reading the entity GET route / underlying Mongo query (routes/[db]/entity/[_id]/index.get.js and its aggregate/property-fetch helpers) would close this gap.

I did not independently confirm from entu-api source that Joosep's live account actually holds editor-but-not-owner on his own section (Soprano II) and lacks _expander on the db entity — that specific rights-assignment fact about the live polyphony/mvox collective data is asserted by Gama's issue triage, not verified by me against the live Entu rights properties on those specific entities. The wire-mechanism explanation (asymmetric rightTypes lists in entity.js vs property/[_id]/index.delete.js) is verified from source and is fully consistent with the reported symptom, but it is not a substitute for reading Joosep's actual _owner/_editor/_expander values on the relevant entities.

Did not trace visibleSiblingsOf's exact filtering logic in full (only referenced it) — if it silently excludes sections the viewer cannot see, the destinationIds passed to reorderSections could differ subtly from the full sibling set; this would only refine, not contradict, the renumber-rights finding above.

This was a read-only investigation per the REPO GUARD; no live Entu calls were made and no code was changed, so all claims about actual runtime behavior (as opposed to code-as-written) are inferences from source, not live-observed traces.

findings.claim: Arrange-mode gate (renders the view-mode chip AND the whole arrange shell with indent/outdent buttons) is a single boolean predicate `admin === 'admin'`, reading rights off the DATABASE ENTITY only — never any section entity.
findings.evidence: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:3029 `{#if admin === 'admin'}` gates the 'Arrange' chip itself; :3046 `{#if viewMode === 'arrange' && admin === 'admin'}` gates the whole arrange-mode shell (indent/outdent buttons rendered inside, e.g. :3096-3097 `canIndent`/`canUnindent`, :3473/:3491 button classes). `admin` = `$derived($adminStore)` (+page.svelte:43). adminStore is populated once per collective-selection by `resolveAdmin(cfg, selected.personId)` at src/routes/+layout.svelte:184-185. resolveAdmin's ENTIRE rights read is `entuFetch(cfg.db, 'entity/${resolvedDbEntityId}?props=_owner,_editor', ...)` (src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts:61-67), returning 'admin' iff personId is in that ONE entity's `_owner` OR `_editor` array (adminStore.ts:84-86). `resolvedDbEntityId` is the collective's DATABASE entity (§161 in comments, adminStore.ts:23-30). No section id is ever read here.

findings.claim: canIndent/canUnindent (the button-enabled predicates) are purely structural — no rights signal at all.
findings.evidence: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:1588-1598: `canIndent(id)` = `prevSiblingId(id) !== null`; `canUnindent(id)` = `findSectionNode(sections, id)?.parentId !== null`. Neither reads any `_owner`/`_editor`/`_expander` value, nor any store. So the ONLY rights gate on the whole arrange feature is the single db-entity `admin==='admin'` check at :3029/:3046 — everything downstream of entering arrange mode is enabled purely by tree shape.

findings.claim: The predicate CAN be true (arrange mode fully rendered, all indent/outdent buttons enabled) while every one of the four underlying writes is denied server-side, because no app code ever grants or even reads rights on individual section entities.
findings.evidence: Rights are granted ONLY on the database entity or the library entity: `addAdmin(cfg, dbEntityId, personId)` → `grantEditor(cfg, dbEntityId, personId)` → POST `[{type:'_editor', reference: personId}]` on `entity/${dbEntityId}` (src/lib/admin/roleManagement.ts:229-255, :324-330); `addLibrarian` is the same shape against `libraryId` (:362-368, :371). Section CREATE never sets `_editor`/`_owner`/`_expander` at all — the create body is 'EXACTLY: _type + _parent + name + _sharing' (src/lib/sections/sectionActions.ts:57-59, :101-... create call), so a section's ONLY explicit rights holder is its own creator, auto-assigned `_owner` at insert time by entu-api (`createEntityRecord`, ~/projects/entu-api/utils/entity.js:404-410 pushes `_owner`+`_created` only, nothing else). No code path (grepped roleManagement.ts, sectionActions.ts) ever POSTs `_editor`/`_owner`/`_expander` onto a section id. Whether a non-creator admin has ANY section rights therefore depends entirely on the `_inheritrights` read-time cascade (entu-api utils/aggregate.js:166-183), which only fires if the section's OWN `_inheritrights` property is `true` — and `createSection`'s body (verified above) never sets `_inheritrights` explicitly, leaving it to entu-api's create-time auto-propagation (`inheritParentProperties`, utils/entity.js:297-326), which only sets it `true` if the PARENT (the database/org entity) itself already has `_inheritrights.boolean===true`. Whether that is actually the live state of the polyphony db entity was not probed this turn — flagged [unverified] below.

findings.claim: Even where the cascade IS active, the four writes split into two different rights requirements at the entu-api level, and the split falls exactly on the reparentSection POST vs DELETE boundary — explaining the reported half-landing.
findings.evidence: Writing the NEW `_parent` value is `POST entity/{sectionId}` → `setEntity` → `checkEntityAccess` (~/projects/entu-api/utils/entity.js:83-121): requires caller in `_editor` OR `_owner` of the section (line 104-111); the SECOND, stricter check (`_owner` required) only fires 'if (rigtsProperties.length > 0)' where `rigtsProperties` is filtered against `rightTypes = ['_noaccess','_viewer','_expander','_editor','_owner','_sharing','_inheritrights']` (entity.js:21-29, line 113) — `_parent` is NOT in that list, so POSTing a new `_parent` needs only editor-or-owner. Deleting the OLD `_parent` value is `DELETE property/{valueId}` → a DIFFERENT route (~/projects/entu-api/routes/[db]/property/[_id]/index.delete.js) whose OWN `rightTypes` list (lines 56-65) DOES include `'_parent'`. So the same editor-or-owner gate applies (lines 129-136) PLUS, because `_parent` is in this route's rightTypes, an ADDITIONAL `_owner`-only gate fires (lines 138-144: 'User not in _owner property'). PLUS a third, independent gate specific to `_parent` deletes (lines 154-179): it looks up the OLD PARENT entity (`property.reference`) and requires the caller be in THAT entity's `_expander` list (line 171, 403 'User not in parent _owner, _editor nor _expander property' otherwise) — a rights check on a THIRD entity that nothing in the app's own rights model (adminStore/roleManagement) ever populates for section-to-section old-parent relationships. Net: an admin who is (inherited-)editor-but-not-owner on a section can always POST a new `_parent` (moves the section) but can never DELETE the stale old `_parent` value (needs owner AND old-parent-expander) — the exact half-landing #264 describes.

findings.claim: This asymmetry is exactly what produces the observed 'nothing landed' lie for indent, because `moveLanded` is only set AFTER the whole reparentSection() call resolves, but the POST inside it already committed before the DELETE throws.
findings.evidence: src/lib/sections/sectionActions.ts `reparentSection` (lines 502-540): GET old `_parent` value ids (512-517) → POST new `_parent` (519-529, commits server-side on 2xx) → loop DELETE each old value id (534-539); any DELETE non-2xx throws `SectionReparentPartialError('reparent', 0, 0, delRes.status, body)` at line 537, AFTER the POST already succeeded. Caller: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte `performReparent` (1627-1697): `await reparentSection(cfg, node.id, newParentId); moveLanded = true;` (1660-1661) — if the awaited call throws (as it does when only the DELETE step fails), line 1661 never runs, so `moveLanded` stays `false` even though the section's `_parent` factually changed server-side. The catch (1668-1692) sets `reparentPartial = moveLanded` (1684) = `false`, and the banner at 2924 renders `m.roster_section_reorder_failed()` = 'The section order couldn't be saved — showing the order the server holds.' (messages/en.json:188) instead of the (accurate, and available) `roster_section_reparent_partial` copy ('The section moved, but its new position couldn't be saved...', en.json:189) — a banner that denies a move the server already made. This matches the issue's Mechanism A exactly, with the DELETE-needs-owner-plus-old-parent-_expander gate (previous finding) as the concrete reason the DELETE step is the one that gets denied while POST succeeds.

findings.claim: SectionReparentPartialError carries step + partial renumber count + raw HTTP status/body, but does NOT distinguish which of GET/POST/DELETE inside the 'reparent' step failed — status alone (403) cannot tell a denied POST (nothing landed) from a denied DELETE (partial landing); only the response body text differs.
findings.evidence: src/lib/sections/sectionErrors.ts:139-156 — `SectionReparentPartialError(step, renumberedCount, totalCount, status, body)`; for ANY of reparentSection's three fetch failures (GET :514, POST :531, DELETE :537) `step` is always `'reparent'` and `renumberedCount`/`totalCount` are always `0`/`0` (sectionActions.ts comment lines 493-495 confirms this explicitly). The three call sites differ only in which `status`+`body` they pass (getRes/postRes/delRes respectively) — e.g. a POST-denied 403 body reads 'User not in _owner nor _editor property' (entity.js:109) while a DELETE-denied 403 body reads either 'User not in _owner property' (property delete.js:143-144, if the owner-only rightTypes gate fired) or 'User not in parent _owner, _editor nor _expander property' (property delete.js:176, if the old-parent-_expander gate fired) — all still HTTP 403. The ONLY console.error sites logging this on the page are +page.svelte:1638 ('roster: section reparent with no cfg'), :1682 ('roster: section reparent failed', e — logs the full error object, not a stringified summary, per the code's own comment at 1671-1682) and :1690 ('roster: section refetch after a failed reparent failed', refetchError). A stage-1 investigator should therefore ask Joosep to expand (not just glance at) the logged Error object at the :1682 console.error site and read its `.step`, `.status`, and especially `.body` fields (the `name`/`code` alone won't disambiguate a POST-denial from a DELETE-denial; only `.body`'s text will) — plus check whether the banner shown was 'roster_section_reorder_failed' (moveLanded read as false) or 'roster_section_reparent_partial' (moveLanded true), since that boolean is itself evidence of which phase (reparentSection vs the later reorderSections renumber) actually raised.

findings.claim: Nothing on the roster page's data-loading path ever fetches rights on a section or member entity — the ONLY rights read anywhere in the load path is the single database-entity `_owner,_editor` GET behind adminStore.
findings.evidence: src/lib/sections/sectionData.ts:95 section list query: `'entity?_type.string=section&props=name,display_order,_parent&limit=500'` — no rights props. src/lib/roster/rosterData.ts:100 member list query: `'entity?_type.string=member&status.string=active&props=person,_parent&limit=500'` — no rights props. Grepped both files plus +page.svelte for `_owner`/`_editor`/`_expander`: the only hit outside comments/adminStore is adminStore.ts's single db-entity GET (already cited above).

risks: [unverified] Whether the live polyphony database entity's OWN `_inheritrights` property is actually `true` or `false`/absent was not probed this turn (read-only guard in effect) — this single fact decides whether Joosep has ANY rights at all on sections he did not create (via the aggregate.js:166-183 cascade), and therefore whether the POST half of reparentSection succeeds for him on a section he doesn't own. If the cascade is NOT active, the earlier symptom would be POST itself 403ing (a different, louder failure than the one reported), so the reported symptom (indent visibly moves) is itself indirect evidence the cascade IS active for this org/db instance — but this inference is [speculative], not confirmed by a source or live read this turn.

[unverified] Which specific section Soprano II's OLD `_parent` pointed at before Joosep's indent (the org/db entity, vs. some other section) was not read from live data — this decides whether the old-parent-_expander gate (entity.js delete route, line 171) or only the owner-only gate (line 140) is the one denying the DELETE. Both are real, source-verified gates; only their live applicability to this exact section pair is unconfirmed.

[unverified] Whether Joosep is literally _editor-not-owner (inherited or direct) on the specific sections involved (Soprano I/II) versus having zero rights on them at all was not probed live — the report's causal chain (editor-sufficient-for-POST, owner-required-for-DELETE) is the best source-grounded explanation for 'POST persists, DELETE denied, banner lies,' but an alternative where BOTH POST and DELETE are denied via the _inheritrights cascade not reaching sections at all (and the observed 'persisted' state came from some other write path, e.g. a stale optimistic UI patch never actually reverted) was not ruled out by a live probe.

[speculative] The reason 'it works under Mihkel (owner)' is most likely that Mihkel personally created (and is thus sole `_owner` of) most/all of the seeded top-level sections, and entu-api's own-entity rights fold (aggregate.js:188-203: owner→editor→expander materialization on the SAME entity) gives him owner+editor+expander on those specific sections directly, sidestepping the whole cascade-and-old-parent-expander question that blocks a granted-not-created admin like Joosep. This was not confirmed against a live seed/creation record this turn.

The fix surface implied by these findings is broader than 'catch the DELETE error better': even a corrected error message would still leave the write DENIED and the section stuck at its old parent's stale reference (or a duplicate _parent value) for any admin who isn't a section's own creator/owner — the structural gap is that arrange-mode's UI gate (db-entity editor-or-owner) has no relationship to what entu-api's write path actually requires per-section (editor for POST _parent, owner AND old-parent-expander for DELETE _parent-value), and no app code currently establishes owner/expander grants on sections for anyone but their creator.

findings.claim: (2) Locale resolution order (client-only, no server): localStorage, then cookie, then preferredLanguage (browser navigator.languages negotiated against the 4 shipped locales), then baseLocale=en as terminal fallback. A fresh/anonymous session only lands on 'en' if none of the first three resolve — i.e. only if the browser's negotiated language isn't one of en/et/lv/uk. An English banner therefore does NOT by itself prove Joosep's setting is en; it is equally consistent with his browser negotiating to something outside the 4 locales, or a prior explicit pick.
findings.evidence: vite.config.ts:21 strategy: ['localStorage','cookie','preferredLanguage','baseLocale']; project.inlang/settings.json baseLocale='en', locales=[en,et,lv,uk]; src/lib/paraglide/runtime.js mirrors the same strategy array (~line 35-39) and implements preferredLanguage via navigator.languages negotiation (~line 825-839) with baseLocale as the final catch (line 659 error text: 'No locale found... Try adding baseLocale as the very last strategy').

findings.claim: (3, decisive) Mechanism A (reparentSection's inner POST of the new _parent succeeds, then its DELETE of the old _parent value is denied, so reparentSection itself throws) IS CONSISTENT with the observed lying 'nothing landed' banner on this codebase: reparentSection's own DELETE-step failure throws SectionReparentPartialError('reparent',0,0,status,body) from inside reparentSection's promise (sectionActions.ts:534-539) — the identical shape a GET failure (line 514) or a POST failure (line 531) would also throw, with no field distinguishing 'POST already landed, only DELETE failed' from 'nothing was sent yet'. findings.claim: A single shared helper `replaceEntityProperty` (src/lib/entu/replaceProperty.ts:40-74) implements the GET-existing → POST-new → DELETE-old choreography with POST-before-DELETE ordering, and throws a plain, untyped `Error` on ANY non-2xx step (lookup GET, POST, or DELETE) with no field distinguishing which step failed or whether the POST already landed.

findings.claim: sectionActions.ts hand-rolls the identical GET→POST→DELETE (POST-before-DELETE) shape three more times outside `reparentSection`: in `reorderSections`'s per-section renumber loop, and in `renameSection`. findings.claim: repertoireActions.ts hand-rolls the same POST-before-DELETE compound-write shape in three functions (`updateRepertoireStatus`, `pinEdition`, `updateProgramItemOrdinal`), all throwing plain untyped Errors indistinguishable by failing step, and the consuming write-queue (`createRepertoireWriteQueue`) does a generic `.catch()` → rollback → revert(key) with zero inspection of which step failed.

findings.claim: A second, REVERSED-order compound-write family exists: `memberLifecycle.ts`'s `flipMemberStatus` (used by deactivate/reinstate), `rsvpData.ts`'s `updateRsvpStatus`, and `attendanceData.ts`'s `updateAttendanceStatus` all do DELETE-old-THEN-POST-new ('clear-then-set'), the opposite order from the POST-before-DELETE house rule elsewhere. A DELETE-succeeds/POST-fails split here leaves the property EMPTY server-side (neither old nor new value) — a distinct, arguably worse half-landing variant than the duplicate-value case the POST-before-DELETE rule was designed to avoid.

findings.claim: Section DELETE ('remove' ✕ on roster) already has a DOCUMENTED instance of the exact 'UI gate broader than the write's actual rights requirement' shape that #264 exhibits: the remove control is gated on `admin === 'admin'` (owner OR editor on the database entity) plus an on-screen emptiness check, but Entu's entity-DELETE endpoint requires `_owner` specifically, and sections are created with NO `_owner`/`_editor`/`_inheritrights` grant beyond Entu's implicit auto-owner-is-creator rule — so any admin who did not personally create the section gets a 403, a case the code comment calls 'not rare'.
findings.evidence: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte:680-689: '#110 review F1 ... Entu only lets `_owner` delete an entity, `_owner` is auto-assigned to the CREATOR, and `createSection`'s body deliberately carries no `_inheritrights` — so an admin who did not personally create the section (every seeded or migration-created one, and every section made by another admin) gets a 403.' findings.claim: The roster page's rights model is structurally BINARY (member vs 'admin'), collapsing owner and editor into one `admin` state via `resolveAdmin`; there is no per-section-editor tier gate anywhere in the roster page. This is the root mechanism behind the rights-tier axis: the arrange UI cannot distinguish 'db owner' from 'db editor' when deciding whether to show a control, even though the underlying Entu writes (entity-DELETE, and per Mechanism B, attaching a `_parent` reference to certain targets) may require owner specifically.
findings.evidence: src/lib/nav/adminStore.ts:84-86: `const isOwner = ...; const isEditor = ...; return isOwner || isEditor ? 'admin' : 'not-admin';` — single OR-merge, type `AdminState = 'loading'|'admin'|'not-admin'|'error'` (line 5). grep of roster/+page.svelte shows every arrange-mode/admin gate (lines 2650, 2815, 3046, 3029, 3565, 3688) keys off this same `admin === 'admin'` boolean, with no second, narrower gate anywhere in the file (grep for section-level _editor/_owner checks in the page returned nothing but a comment at 3049).

findings.claim: Sections are created WITHOUT setting `_inheritrights: true`, while member entities ARE created with `_inheritrights: true` explicitly — an asymmetry that plausibly explains why db-level owner/editor rights propagate onto members (making deactivate/reinstate reliably gated by the `admin` boolean) but do NOT reliably propagate onto sections (making section writes exposed to the creator-only-owner gap regardless of the acting person's db-level tier).
findings.evidence: src/lib/sections/sectionActions.ts:148-153 — createSection's full create body is `_type + _parent + name + _sharing` only, no `_inheritrights` key. src/lib/invite/inviteData.ts:286-290 — member create body explicitly includes `{ type: '_inheritrights', boolean: true }` (with surrounding comment at 279-281 confirming this is deliberate so the member 'lands `domain`... already' via inheritance). src/lib/admin/roleManagement.ts:8-16 module comment independently confirms Entu's aggregated rights read splices in PARENT rights only 'via the inherit-rights link' — i.e. inheritance is conditional on `_inheritrights`, corroborating that sections (no such flag) do not get the splice non-creators would need.

findings.claim: Given the above, the #264 Mechanism-B framing ('outdent target is the org/db entity, and writing a `_parent` ref to it needs rights Joosep lacks') is consistent with — but not fully explained by — the codebase: I can verify the STRUCTURAL asymmetry (sections don't inherit db rights; members do; DELETE needs owner specifically), but I cannot verify from static code alone whether Entu's authorization for `POST _parent: <ref>` additionally checks rights on the REFERENCED TARGET entity (which would explain why indent, targeting a sibling SECTION, succeeds for an editor while outdent, targeting the DB entity, fails) versus some other db-entity-specific policy (e.g. the db/organization type requiring owner-tier for any attach). This distinction needs a live probe against Entu, not a code read.
findings.evidence: No direct code path in this repo evaluates or asserts Entu's server-side authorization rule for a reference-typed property write against its target entity's rights — that logic lives in Entu itself, outside this repo. Flagging as [speculative]/[unverified] per task instructions rather than asserting a specific Entu mechanism.

findings.claim: The two structural-write functions under #253/#264 review (`performReorder` and `performReparent` in roster/+page.svelte) check the `routeLoad.generation` mid-collective-switch guard ONLY on their failure/refetch branch, never on their success branch — unlike the deactivate-reload path, which was explicitly patched (#259) to add this guard specifically because 'the await can outlive a mid-flight collective switch.' The underlying Entu writes are not misrouted to the wrong db (cfg is captured synchronously, before any switch could occur), but a late-arriving SUCCESS for section reorder/reparent after a collective switch would still write `reorderStatus`/`sections` state with no generation check, unlike every other guarded write path in this file.
findings.evidence: src/routes/roster/+page.svelte: performReorder — `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at line 1530, success branch (lines 1541-1548, `await reorderSections(...)`, `reorderStatus = ...`, `return true;`) has NO `g`/`routeLoad.isCurrent` check; the guard appears ONLY in the catch branch at line 1554 (`if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return false;`). performReparent — same shape: `const g = routeLoad.generation;` at line 1643, success branch at 1659-1667 (`await reparentSection(...)`, `await reorderSections(...)`, `reorderStatus = announce(); return true;`) has no generation check; guard only appears in the catch branch at line 1687. Contrast with handleDeactivateConfirm, which captures `g` AFTER its own write specifically to guard its post-write reload (lines 808-825: '#259 ... this reload's cfg was captured well before this await, and the await can outlive a mid-flight collective switch ... Guarded via the route-load machine's external co-guard seam'). This is a verified code-level asymmetry; whether it manifests as user-visible corruption depends on how `sections`/`currentDbEntityId` are reset on collective switch, which I did not trace end-to-end this turn — flagging the SUCCESS-BRANCH GAP as verified, and its downstream blast radius as [unverified].

findings.claim: sectionActions.partial.spec.ts already contains a unit-level test that exercises the EXACT #264 Mechanism-A scenario ('an old-parent DELETE fails after the POST landed') and asserts it produces the SAME error shape (step:'reparent', renumberedCount:0, totalCount:0) as a pure lookup-GET failure ('nothing written at all') — i.e. the spec pins that `reparentSection`'s thrown error carries NO signal distinguishing 'POST already landed, only cleanup failed' from 'nothing was written'. A stage-2 fix that disambiguates these (e.g. adding a `postLanded`/similar field) will have to change this spec's expected shape.

findings.claim: page.roster-indent.spec.ts contains the PAGE-LEVEL test that pins the actual lying banner/revert behavior #264 reports live: when `reparentSection` rejects with a `step:'reparent'` error (status 403, body 'forbidden by rights' — the SAME shape a POST-landed/DELETE-denied inner failure produces per the unit spec above), the test asserts the tree REVERTS to depth 0 (as if nothing landed) and the banner shows `roster_section_reorder_failed` (the 'nothing changed' copy), explicitly NOT `roster_section_reparent_partial`. This is the concrete 'currently PIN the lying behavior' test asked for in task item (5).

findings.claim: By contrast, the sibling PIN for the OUTER #253 pair (reparent lands, then reorderSections/renumber fails) is already correctly truthful — it asserts the section renders AT ITS NEW DEPTH and shows the landed-move copy, not a revert. This shows the team already fixed the ANALOGOUS ambiguity one level up (between reparentSection succeeding vs reorderSections failing) but has not yet extended the same fix INSIDE reparentSection itself (between its own POST landing vs its own DELETE being denied) — which is precisely the stage-2 scope.
findings.evidence: src/routes/page.roster-indent.spec.ts:792-842, test 'a reparent that LANDS but whose sibling RENUMBER fails reconciles to the TRUTH...' — rejects `reorderMock` (not `reparentMock`) with a `step:'renumber'` error and asserts `data-depth` becomes '1' (landed) and banner contains `roster_section_reparent_partial`, not `roster_section_reorder_failed` (lines 822-839). risks: Entu's server-side authorization rule for why a reference write (`_parent` POST) might additionally require rights on the TARGET entity (explaining indent-succeeds/outdent-fails for an editor) is inferred from structural asymmetry (sections lack `_inheritrights`, DELETE requires owner) but not confirmed by a live probe against the Entu API — this is the single largest unverified link in the Mechanism-B chain and should be probe-verified before stage 2 design locks in a fix.

The generation-guard gap on performReorder/performReparent's success branch (finding 8) is verified at the code level, but I did not trace how `sections`/`currentDbEntityId`/`routeLoad` actually reset on a collective switch end-to-end, so its real user-visible blast radius (does a stale success banner actually reach the screen, or is it masked by an unrelated re-render) is unverified and could be smaller or larger than it appears.

This sweep covered replaceEntityProperty callers, sectionActions.ts, repertoireActions.ts, memberLifecycle/rsvp/attendance status-flip functions, and the roster/event-detail rights gates — it did NOT audit invite/inviteData.ts, profile/profileData.ts, eventConvert.ts, or seasonManage.ts's own DELETE call sites (only grepped their existence) for the same half-landing shape; those remain unchecked and could contain further instances.

The rights-tier enumeration (member / section-editor / org-owner) found only a de facto TWO-tier model (not-admin / admin) on the roster page's own gating; whether the schema genuinely supports a third 'section-editor' tier anywhere else in the app (e.g. a section entity ever explicitly granted `_editor` to a non-creator, non-db-admin person) was not fully verified — I found no code path that grants or checks it, but that is an absence-of-evidence finding, not a proof it cannot occur via manual Entu-side grants outside the app's own write paths.

Time/effort budget meant several call sites (renameSection's plain-Error shape, updateAttendanceStatus's exact line numbers, roleManagement.ts write paths) were confirmed to exist and share the pattern by structure/grep but not read to the same line-by-line depth as the primary findings above.
